prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M; scope: offshore assets, marine/shore facilities, personnel, external orgs, electrical up to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere: farm/transmission boundary, exchanges authorized signals with transmission system, normal-supply/protection status); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): executes authorized control, limits output, blocks protection-conflicting commands, reports state, safe mode on auxiliary loss; produces Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (interlocks), Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur): imagery. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable to grid point, Export Cable Monitor (export-path measurements), station service transformers (essential/nonessential separated). Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-starts on auxiliary loss, transfers to emergency bus only within V/f limits, no unapproved paralleling, no export; sheds nonessential on overload; failure→alarm, keep UPS power; transfer back only when stable and safely unloadable. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): status, alarms, relay status/interface measurements to Shore Control Room (Amber Quay, coordinates notices/interface decisions); flags work from Pitch Deviation Notice; produces Session Revocation Receipt on session termination. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): schedules by condition/history, periodic standby-electrical reviews, uses Squall Window Bulletin. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): allocates output among units; commands limited by capability/protection/limits. Grid Dispatcher sets dispatch per connection agreement. Farm reports boundary active power; reactive per agreement; frequency response only if mode authorized; protection coordination avoids needless trips; comms loss keeps protection/interlocks; Grid Constraint→reduce/redispatch/disconnect; alarms prioritized safety>protection>export; tests avoid dispatch/maintenance conflicts. Crew Transfer Vessel (Kestrel Bay, reports approach/departure), Daughter Craft, SOV, Helideck. Vessel AIS Receiver (Blue Granite): Position Quality Flag. Personnel Tracking Console, North/South Access Scanners. Warehouse System (Mosslight): Backorder Exception Slip; Spares Hub. Metocean Buoy (Copper Finch): Wave Burst Record. Cybersecurity Gateway (Quiet Harbor): deny-by-default, RBAC, logged sessions. Work Permit Portal (Redoubt): records lifecycle, audit. Permit: Duty Planner (Transfer Manifest Addendum) submits→HSE Officer, reviewers, Marine Coordinator, Vessel

New part:
S220: A return to normal export follows confirmation that the interface is stable and all required protections are available.
S221: The Grid Interface Relay maintains the farm's dispatch boundary while allowing local systems to manage turbine-level operation.
S222: Marine coordination aligns vessel movements, personnel transfers, and shore-side support with the approved work schedule.
S223: The Marine Coordinator maintains the daily marine plan and resolves conflicts between planned activities.
S224: The Duty Planner updates work priorities when access conditions or resource availability change.
S225: The Fleet Dispatch Console uses the quality flag to support movement planning.
S226: The Vessel Master confirms departure readiness and reports any change that could affect the passage.
S227: The Crew Transfer Vessel is assigned to transfers that meet the approved operating limits.
S228: The Service Operations Vessel provides a stable offshore base when the work plan requires extended support.
S229: The Daughter Craft is used only when its task, route, and operating conditions have been reviewed.
S230: The Weather Service provides forecast information for marine planning.
S231: Copper Finch reports local sea conditions for use in access planning.
S232: The Weather Analyst reviews forecast changes and advises the Marine Coordinator when conditions may affect the plan.
S233: Weather Hold is applied when environmental limits make a planned movement or transfer unsafe.
S234: The Personnel Tracking Console maintains the offshore personnel roster and expected return times.
S235: The North Access Scanner records authorized entry at the north access point.
S236: The South Access Scanner records authorized entry at the south access point.
S237: The HSE Officer produces the Harness Audit Card before the applicable transfer activity.
S238: The Shore Control Room maintains an overview of active marine operations and operational restrictions.
S239: The Operations Radio Console supports routine communications and escalation during offshore activity.
S240: The Port Agent coordinates port services and confirms that planned departures can be supported.
S241: Mosslight records stock movements and makes current inventory information available for logistics planning.
S242: The Storekeeper prepares requested equipment for dispatch in accordance with the approved work plan.
S243: The Work Permit Portal is checked before personnel are released to perform controlled work offshore.
S244: The Rescue Coordinator maintains the response arrangements for incidents involving vessels or personnel.
S245: The Marine Coordinator records changes to the movement plan and ensures that affected teams receive the update.
S246: The Maintenance Planning Engine ranks planned and corrective work using asset condition, safety exposure, production impact, access feasibility, and resource availability.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
